title: Candidate controller
summary: Release-run QA runs controller-side work (host control, mission preparation, walker mission commands) on the run's candidate Yoke build. After begin and before any host lease, an execution whose frozen target names an installer origin compares the controller's build commit with the candidate: the release_lineage the target's channel serves, or the release the deployed commit pins. A stale controller installs the candidate wheels into a private runtime under the Yoke machine home, never touching the installed CLI or its channel, and hands it the begun execution; walker commands name that runtime's executable. After a takeover, the target the controller checks names the owning run's release_lineage once that run has a ready deploy receipt for the target's source stage, so a moved execution that already recorded a case still begins; its stored target and digest stay unchanged. A channel serving another build than that release_lineage refuses naming the run and build from that target, and the owning run when a takeover moved it; the command first begins the execution again in place up to three times, 20 seconds apart, so an unbegun execution takes its owning run's current target and keeps its queue place, and only a target that stays stale releases it. A runtime that cannot be provisioned refuses qa_controller_not_candidate with installed and candidate versions, aborts the unused execution and names the recovery. Machine and mission preparation evidence record controller_runtime with its source_commit.
